source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Nameless, it is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; named, it is the mother of the myriad things.
Therefore, always free from desire, one can observe its subtlety,
and always with desire, one can observe its outer limit;
These two arise together yet bear different names; together they are called the mysterious.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a road, route, or means of going from one place or state to another
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete spatial sense, common outside philosophical texts.
Sentence Translations (English): The road is far, and one cannot go alone.
He lost the road and did not know where to return.
A broad road is level and easy to travel.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to put something into words or state it aloud
additional_senses.Nuance (English): In philosophical prose, this can shade into ‘to express’ or ‘to formulate’ rather than casual speech.
Sentence Translations (English): I do not dare state the details.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the fundamental principle or course by which things arise and operate; here, the ultimate Way discussed in the Laozi
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often also implies an ordering principle or path, not just a named doctrine.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to regard something as proper, right, or worthy of approval
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often used in judgments of rightness, not just practical possibility.
Sentence Translations (English): The crowd all approved his proposal.
His words were acceptable and should be followed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): indicates possibility, permission, or suitability for the action that follows
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks what can legitimately or effectively be done, not mere factual ability.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): used in judgments of correctness or identity, often contrasting what is true with what merely seems so
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Common in set contrasts such as 非……也, meaning ‘is not truly…’ or ‘is not the case that…’.
Sentence Translations (English): He is not the right person.
It is not what I want.
This is not a small matter.
I dare not disobey the order.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): negates the following word or clause
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often carries a sharper contrast or correction than 不.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the usual, regular pattern or normal order of things
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Refers to what is normally expected, not the Laozi’s metaphysical sense.
Sentence Translations (English): Human affairs have their usual course.
Worldly matters follow the regular order.
His conduct accords with the normal course.
The ordinary order must not be disturbed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a fixed, regular, or permanent way; here, the permanent Dao as distinct from a speakable Dao
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Contrasts the enduring, universal Dao with any particular describable instance or formulation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the standing or renown a person or thing has among others
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A social sense very common in early texts.
Sentence Translations (English): His name was known in all directions.
The credit goes to the lord.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the act of giving a designation, or the designation itself as applied to things
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it points to verbal designation, not merely a label as an object.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a lasting fame or standing that does not quickly change
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used of reputation or memorial lasting over time.
Sentence Translations (English): Loyalty and righteousness leave a lasting reputation.
His enduring fame has not faded.
A lasting reputation is established in the world.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a fixed, permanent designation, contrasted with a name that can be spoken and assigned
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks a name treated as stable and ultimate, not merely any ordinary label.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): negates existence, possession, or presence
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Very common negation of existence or possession.
Sentence Translations (English): There is no one in the room.
There are no troops in the city.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the state of lacking a designation, and by extension the undifferentiated condition before distinctions arise
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is philosophically loaded: not merely ‘there is none,’ but an undifferentiated starting condition.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the sky above and the earth below as the broad world of nature
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete cosmological or natural-world reference.
Sentence Translations (English): Heaven and earth are a witness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the paired totality of heaven and earth, used as a standard way to refer to the whole ordered world
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A cosmological pair, not two ordinary physical objects.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a pronominal particle sometimes used for reference or nominalization in classical prose
additional_senses.Nuance (English): In many classical contexts it serves grammatical rather than lexical function.
Sentence Translations (English): To know it as knowing it.
To learn without weariness and teach without fatigue—what is there in me? I do not blame it.
Sentences: 學而不厭，誨人不倦，何有於我哉？非之也。

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a grammatical marker linking nouns, often indicating possession, attribution, or nominal modification
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A highly flexible genitive/attributive particle in Classical Chinese.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to start an action or process
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Common verbal sense, distinct from the noun ‘beginning’.
Sentence Translations (English): The king began to use force.
The people at last became settled.
Only then can it be known.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the initial point or origin of a process or state
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Emphasizes the first arising or inception of something.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to have as one’s own or to be in possession of
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often overlaps with existential ‘there is’.
Sentence Translations (English): I have one point to make.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): marks existence or possession
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Simply indicates presence or possession; in philosophical contrast with 無, it marks manifested being.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): all entities taken together, without emphasis on cosmological theory
additional_senses.Nuance (English): General collective sense, common in early texts.
Sentence Translations (English): Observe the changes of all things.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the totality of created or manifest things in the world
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A comprehensive cosmological term for the multiplicity of beings and things.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): the woman who bears and raises a child
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Literal kinship sense.
Sentence Translations (English): The mother has recovered from illness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): that which gives birth to or produces something; here, the source from which all things arise
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often used figuratively for a generative source, not only a literal parent.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): refers to something from earlier times or an earlier condition
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Very common lexical sense, distinct from the connective.
Sentence Translations (English): The mountains and rivers of the former state.
His aspiration was still the same as before.
The old clothes are still there.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): introduces a conclusion or result based on what has just been said
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks inference from preceding premises, not mere temporal sequence.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): unchanging or recurring in an orderly way
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used of stable patterns, seasons, or norms.
Sentence Translations (English): The four seasons have their regular course.
The established law must not be discarded.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): continuous or habitual, not interrupted or occasional
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Describes an ongoing condition or repeated habit.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to want something or be inclined toward it
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Common verbal use.
Sentence Translations (English): I do not wish to speak much.
He wanted to go but stopped.
What do you seek, my lord?

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a wanting or craving for something
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In the Laozi this often carries the sense of desire as a source of disturbance or partiality.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to take something as a means or instrument
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A common older verbal sense, distinct from the preposition.
Sentence Translations (English): What shall we use as a plan?

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): introduces the means, method, or purpose by which an action is carried out
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In classical usage this can mark means, basis, or purpose depending on context.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text
contextual_sense.Translation (English): by means of; in order to

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to see or watch something with the eyes
additional_senses.Nuance (English): More concrete visual sense.
Sentence Translations (English): He climbed the platform to look at it.
Remain still and watch the changes.
Sit and look at the writings.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to look at attentively in order to perceive or understand
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here the act is not casual seeing but reflective apprehension.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a distal demonstrative referring to something already mentioned or understood
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Can function demonstratively in some classical passages.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a third-person possessive or attributive pronoun referring to the thing previously mentioned
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Usually broad and context-dependent, ranging from ‘its’ to ‘their’ or ‘that’.﻿
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): extraordinarily fine, elusive, or impressive in quality
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often describes skill or workmanship as exquisite or marvelous.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the fine, elusive, profound quality of what cannot be easily grasped or fully described
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Suggests subtle profundity rather than mere prettiness or cleverness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to examine or measure something carefully, especially by going to its edge or limit
additional_senses.Nuance (English): An older verbal sense found in texts of measurement, regulation, and inspection.
Sentence Translations (English): Examine it to learn its extent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the limit, verge, or boundary of something
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Refers to an outer limit or boundary, not a frontier in the modern administrative sense.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): refers to the present place, time, or situation
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Common deictic use.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a Way in this.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a distal or proximal demonstrative referring to something just mentioned or present in the discourse
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Points to the items already under discussion.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): two considered together as a pair or combined whole
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Common in paired or mutually related reference.
Sentence Translations (English): The two states are at peace with each other.
The two matters are raised together.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the number immediately greater than one
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Used for a paired or dual count, often after demonstratives or classifiers.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a general nominal suffix used to form a referent from a description
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Very common in Classical Chinese as a flexible marker of the referent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a nominalizing or relative particle marking a person or thing described by the preceding phrase
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Turns what precedes into a substantive reference, often ‘the one(s) that…’.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to go along with, accompany, or act in concert with
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A verbal sense common in early prose.
Sentence Translations (English): I wish to go with you.
All the others agreed with it.
Cross together in the same boat.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): indicates sameness, concordance, or acting in the same way
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it marks shared origin or shared characterization before the following predicates.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to move from inside to outside or leave a place
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete spatial sense.
Sentence Translations (English): When the sun rises, we set out.
Someone came out at the gate.
He may not leave the city.
He went out and came back in.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to issue forth, arise, or come from a source
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In cosmological prose it often means ‘originate from’ rather than merely ‘go out’.﻿
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): marks succession or result between actions or states
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often more sequential than strictly additive.
Sentence Translations (English): Learn and then reflect on it.
He heard it and understood it.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): joins two clauses or predicates in a loose coordinated or sequential relation
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In Classical Chinese it can mark sequence, contrast, or simple coordination depending on context.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to make or become different
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Common verbal sense.
Sentence Translations (English): Times change and matters become different.
It is different, yet not harmful.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): not the same in kind, name, or characterization
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks genuine difference rather than mere variation in degree.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): to regard or judge something as being a certain way
additional_senses.Nuance (English): A very common evaluative use.
Sentence Translations (English): What do you think of it?
I think it can be done.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): to designate or refer to something in speech or thought
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Often has the sense ‘call’ or ‘say that X is Y’.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi/Wang Bi text
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to call; to speak of as

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): of a dark color or dim appearance
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concrete color sense.
Sentence Translations (English): The dark color was very deep.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a deeply subtle, dark, or ineffable state or quality beyond ordinary distinction
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In the Laozi it suggests profound hiddenness and ungraspable depth, not mere darkness.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; Laozi base text as transmitted in the Wang Bi recension
